title: Spec-derived VCF 9.1 fleet install in Go that survives an access token expiring mid-run
prompt:
We ship `vcf-fleet-run`, an internal tool that installs VMware Cloud Foundation
9.1 fleet components through the SDDC LCM service and then tells the operator
exactly what happened. A run is long: resolving binaries from the Fleet depot and
deploying appliances takes far longer than an access token lives, so the token
expires part way through and the run has to carry on from where it was. Re-doing
work the service has already accepted would deploy an appliance twice.

The repository already has the example plan, a loopback mock of the service, a
tool for driving that mock by hand and the contract test. The derived REST
contract and the run itself are missing. Build them.

Everything runs on the Go standard library. Do not add a requirement to
`go.mod`, and do not vendor an HTTP, YAML or assertion library. `fleetrun` and
`cmd` must not import `internal/mocklcm` or `contracttest`.

## 1. Derive the REST contract from the specification

The contract must come from the OpenAPI specification itself, not from a
rendered documentation page, an SDK, or recollection. Read
`specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml` in the `vmware/vcf-api-specs`
repository on GitHub (Apache-2.0) at commit
`c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`, and write `docs/contract.json`
describing exactly the five operations this tool calls, named by their
operationIds:

    getComponents, resolveDepotComponents, createComponents, getTask, retryTask

The file has exactly these five keys:

    {
      "source": {"repository", "specPath", "commit", "license",
                 "openapi", "apiTitle", "apiVersion"},
      "server": "<the server URL the spec publishes>",
      "security": {"scheme", "type", "httpScheme", "bearerFormat"},
      "operations": {"<operationId>": {...}},
      "schemas": {"<schemaName>": {"required": [...], "optional": [...]}}
    }

* `source.repository` is `owner/name`, `specPath` is the path above, `commit` is
  that commit, `license` is the repository's SPDX identifier, and `openapi` /
  `apiTitle` / `apiVersion` are the spec's `openapi` version, `info.title` and
  `info.version`.
* `security` describes the single security scheme the spec defines: its name
  under `securitySchemes` as `scheme`, its `type`, its HTTP `scheme` as
  `httpScheme` spelled exactly as the spec spells it, and its `bearerFormat`.
* Each entry of `operations` has exactly these keys: `method` (upper case),
  `path` (the spec's path template, parameters kept as `{name}`),
  `successStatus` (the 2xx status the operation documents), `requestSchema` (the
  name of the request body schema, or `null` when the operation takes no body),
  `responseSchema` (the schema of the success response), `pathParams`,
  `fixedQuery`, `queryParams` as `{"required": [...], "optional": [...]}`, and
  `optionalHeaders` (the header parameters the operation declares).
* One of these operations is written in the spec with a query parameter pinned
  to a constant inside the path key itself. That constant belongs in
  `fixedQuery`, as an object mapping the parameter to its value, and must not be
  left in `path`. `fixedQuery` is `{}` for an operation that pins none, and a
  parameter pinned there is not also listed under `queryParams`.
* The one operation whose request body the spec defines as a discriminated
  `oneOf` carries one further key, `requestVariants`, as
  `{"discriminator": "<the discriminator property>", "variants": [...]}` naming
  the values the discriminator selects between.
* `schemas` gives the required/optional field split, exactly as the spec marks
  it, for every schema a request body may be built against: the request schema
  of `resolveDepotComponents` and the two schemas it nests, the request schema
  of `createComponents`, the variant of its discriminated item that describes
  importing an existing component, and the schema of that variant's optional
  repository object. Six schemas in all.
* Every list of strings in the file is sorted lexicographically.

Record where it came from in `docs/official_sources.json`:

    {"sources": [{"title", "repository", "path", "commit", "url", "rawUrl",
                  "license", "retrieved", "sha256", "operationIds"}]}

`repository` is the `https://github.com/...` URL, `path` is the spec path, `url`
and `rawUrl` are permalinks pinned to that commit, `sha256` is the digest of the
specification file at that commit, `retrieved` is an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` date, and
`operationIds` lists the five operationIds above, sorted.

The mock builds its route table from `docs/contract.json` and serves only the
operations the contract names. It checks each request against the contract too:
a query parameter or body field the contract does not declare, a missing
required field, a field sent empty, a header the operation does not declare or
the wrong success status all come back as an error. A contract that disagrees
with the specification therefore produces a service that rejects the client.

## 2. The fleetrun package

Write package `fleetrun` in `fleetrun/`, exporting:

    type Options struct {
        PlanPath     string           // the install plan to carry out
        ContractPath string           // the derived REST contract
        BaseURL      string           // the SDDC LCM service to drive
        Credentials  CredentialSource // supplies and replaces the access token
        PollInterval time.Duration    // zero means 5 seconds
        PollTimeout  time.Duration    // zero means 1 hour
        HTTPClient   *http.Client     // nil means a default client
    }

    type CredentialSource interface {
        Token(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
        Refresh(ctx context.Context, expired string) (string, error)
    }

    func Run(ctx context.Context, opts Options) (*Report, error)

`ContractPath` empty means `docs/contract.json`. `Run` returns an error only
when the run could not be carried out at all: an unusable plan or contract, a
component the depot does not carry, an answer it cannot make sense of, a
credential that could not be replaced, or a task that never settled. An install
that fails is a result, not an error, and is described by the report. `Report`
is your type; it must marshal to the JSON described below. `Run` must be safe to
call concurrently for different `Options`.

Also export `StaticCredential`, a `CredentialSource` backed by a fixed string
whose `Refresh` fails because there is nothing to refresh to.

Read the URL, method, success status, parameter placement and required/optional
field split out of the contract at run time rather than hard-coding them.

Every request carries the credential the contract's security scheme calls for:
`Authorization: <httpScheme> <token>`. Bodies are sent as `application/json`.
When the plan supplies a `correlationId`, send it as the `X-Correlation-Id`
header on the operations that declare that header — and only on those.

## 3. The command line tool

Write `cmd/vcf-fleet-run`:

    vcf-fleet-run -plan PATH -base-url URL -report PATH
        (-token TOKEN | -token-file PATH)
        [-contract PATH] [-poll-interval D] [-poll-timeout D]

`-contract` defaults to `docs/contract.json`, `-poll-interval` to `5s` and
`-poll-timeout` to `1h`. `-token` is a single credential that cannot be renewed;
`-token-file` holds the credentials provisioned for the run, one per line, and
refreshing advances to the next. Exactly one of the two is required. It writes
the report to `-report`, prints a short human-readable summary to stdout naming
every planned component, the task and how often the credential was refreshed,
and exits 0 when the install succeeded, 1 when it failed, and 2 when the plan,
the contract, the credentials or the service made the run impossible.

## 4. Plan format

`fixtures/install-plan.json` is an example:

* `scope`: optional component scope filter.
* `correlationId`: optional.
* `depot`: required, with a required `fqdn` and `certificate`.
* `depotVersion`: optional, the depot release version to resolve against.
* `binaryCertificate`: optional, the certificate the binary repository presents.
* `components`: an ordered, non-empty list of components with distinct
  `componentType`. Each entry has a required `componentType`, `fqdn` and
  `password`, and optional `version`, `username`, `size`, `sslThumbprint` and
  `vmId`.

## 5. Steps, in this order

1. `getComponents`, narrowed by the plan's `scope` when it sets one, to learn
   what is already installed. A planned component whose `componentType` the
   inventory already carries is skipped.
2. If nothing is left to install, stop. Raising a task would be work invented.
3. `resolveDepotComponents` for the components that are left, in plan order,
   asking the plan's depot to turn each `componentType` — and the entry's
   `version` when it pins one — into a binary. A component the depot does not
   answer for makes the run impossible.
4. `createComponents` once, carrying one import spec per remaining component in
   plan order. Each spec uses the discriminator value that selects the import
   variant, and carries the component's type, fqdn and password, the version the
   depot resolved, and the plan's optional per-component fields. The resolved
   binary and the plan's `binaryCertificate` go on the spec's optional
   repository object.
5. Poll `getTask` until the task reaches a terminal state. `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`
   and `CANCELED` are terminal; `PENDING`, `SCHEDULED` and `RUNNING` are not.
   The answer that raised the task does not settle it, whatever status it
   carries. Wait `PollInterval` between polls and give up after `PollTimeout`.
6. If the task ended `FAILED` and the service says it is retriable, call
   `retryTask` once and poll it out again. Do not retry a second time, and do
   not retry a task the service does not mark retriable.

## 6. When the credential expires

The service answers `401` when the access token it was given has expired. That
is not the end of the run:

* Refresh the credential once, passing the rejected one to `Refresh`, and send
  the very same request again with the replacement.
* Refresh only in answer to a rejection. A credential that is still good is
  never replaced, and nothing is refreshed ahead of time.
* If the replacement is rejected too, give up with an error rather than
  refreshing round and round.
* If `Refresh` fails, give up with an error. Do not push on with a credential
  the service has already rejected.
* Nothing above the request layer learns that the credential changed. Work the
  service has already accepted is never re-sent: a rejected poll is polled
  again, not turned into a second install.

## 7. Sending optional fields

An optional field with no value is omitted from the request, never sent empty.
If the plan sets no `scope`, no query string is sent at all — not a bare `?` and
not an empty parameter. A plan entry that pins no version sends no version. If
the plan sets no `correlationId`, the header is absent rather than empty. If the
depot published no binary and the plan carries no `binaryCertificate`, the
optional repository object has nothing to hold and is left off entirely, rather
than sent as `{}` or `null`. A field the spec marks required is always sent.

## 8. The report

    {
      "outcome": "succeeded" | "failed",
      "scope": "<the plan's scope, absent when it sets none>",
      "skipped": ["<componentType>"],
      "installed": [{"componentType", "fqdn", "version", "downloadUrl"}],
      "task": {"id", "status", "retried"},
      "credentialRefreshes": <count>,
      "failure": {"taskId", "failedStage",
                  "errors": [{"id", "defaultMessage"}]}
    }

`outcome`, `skipped`, `installed` and `credentialRefreshes` are always present;
`skipped` and `installed` are in plan order and may be empty. `scope` is absent
when the plan sets none. `installed` describes the components that were
submitted, carrying the version the depot resolved and the binary it published;
`downloadUrl` is absent for a component the depot published no binary for.
`task` is absent when no task was raised, and `retried` says whether
`retryTask` was called. `credentialRefreshes` counts how often the access token
had to be replaced.

`outcome` is `succeeded` when no install task was needed or when the task reached
`SUCCEEDED`. Otherwise it is `failed` and `failure` names the task, the name of the task stage the service
marked failed and that stage's `ERROR` level messages by `id` and
`defaultMessage` — those only. When no stage is marked failed, `failedStage` is
absent and the errors are the task's own `ERROR` level messages. `failure` is
absent from a report that succeeded, and the report carries no keys beyond these.

## Checking your work

    bash verify.sh

builds the module, vets it and runs `go test -race ./contracttest/...`, which
starts the mock on loopback, drives the run against it and inspects every
recorded request: the target, the method, the credential presented, the headers
and the exact JSON body. `go.mod`, `README.md`, `verify.sh`, `fixtures/`,
`internal/`, `tools/` and `contracttest/` are fixed inputs; do not edit them.
You can also drive the mock by hand — see README.md.

network.reason: The REST contract must be derived from specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository on github.com, which the agent fetches itself. Verification is offline and contacts no VMware endpoint.

prerequisites.notes: go test -race needs cgo and a C toolchain.
